newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European markets pause, consolidate gains.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European markets pause, consolidate gains.

text.p: Most European stock markets paused on Thursday to consolidate recent record highs, but Finnish shares jumped to an all-time high with help from impressive earnings from telecoms group Ericsson.

The dollar spiked above 1.83 marks again after Germany's central bank kept interest rates steady, as expected, at its last meeting before a summer recess and made no references to the strong dollar. The dollar continues to linger near six-year highs against the mark.
Stocks were mixed, consolidating recent runs to record peaks, but Finnish shares managed to break out to an all-time high.

Finland's FOX index started cautiously higher but extended gains to a record peak after Ericsson surged about 12 percent on impressive first-half results. Ericsson said pre-tax profits gained 44 percent versus a year ago.

Germany's DAX index, Europe's forerunner in the race this week to all-time highs, ignored the Bundesbank's rate decision and held sharply lower levels at midday as banking shares fell on corporate earnings. The DAX and several other European bourses hit record peaks on Wednesday after Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan predicted moderate economic growth amid low inflation this year in the U.S. in his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony.

Commerzbank AG and Vereins- und Westbank AG fell after first-half results. By midmorning, Commerzbank was down three marks at 62.00 despite higher-than-expected earnings. Commerzbank said first-half operating profits rose 23.2 percent.
Vereinsbank shares tumbled 14 marks to 101.00 on lower-than-expected earnings. Its operating profit rose 15.2 percent in the first half.
Despite the DAX's slip, traders remained upbeat on the index, saying the dollar's continued strength and Wall Street's higher close overnight would keep the market underpinned.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed up 26.71 points at 8,088.36.
Dutch shares, which also posted a record high on Wednesday, lost ground by midday despite an earlier boost from Philips Electronics NV's strong second-quarter earnings.

Philips shares jumped more than eight percent to a year high of 177 after the company said second-quarter net profits from ordinary operations rose to 693 million guilders, outpacing analysts' expectations between 429 and 540 million.
French stocks recovered early losses made when investors sold shares to lock in profits made in this week's jump to record highs.

In London, the FTSE-100 index traded choppily. It opened lower but rose on a smaller-than-expected British May trade deficit. The deficit tallied 508 million sterling, sharply lower than April's 989 million and forecasts for 960 million.

But a Confederation of British Industry survey in late morning helped pare gains. The CBI said export orders fell at their fastest rate since October 1991 in the four months to July, while domestic demand grew at its fastest rate since April 1995. It predicted overall demand would grow strongly in the next four months but warned a near-term rate rise would be "unwelcome."
CURRENCIES AT 1135 GMT
The dollar was at 1.8335 marks and 115.70 yen compared to 1.8235 and 115.73 in late trading on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1135 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 9.4 points at 4,883.9.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index was down 65.87 points, or 1.5 percent, in bourse trade at 4,340.22.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 1.86 points at 3,005.39.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $321.80 per ounce in the morning from Wednesday's fix at $324.90. Silver opened down at $4.28 from the last close at $4.32.
